quote: The central bank does not have access to customer data and does not have responsibility for AML/KYC/CTF, but through its own roles it has access to aggregated overviews of circulation, holdings, and transaction activity on the ledger.
transaction_scope: online retail CBDC sandbox (test case 1, Hyperledger Besu)
modality: conditional: pseudonymous ledger addresses; identity mapping held only by banks
justification: In the tested retail sandbox, banks hold the identity-to-address mapping and the CB sees only pseudonymous ledger data and aggregates. The CB therefore holds no routine key to identity in this tested design. Doc 6 p.16 says Norges Bank 'should not have information' about individual holdings, but that is a 'will not see' statement in a design list called a rough draft. Norges Bank decided in Dec 2025 not to introduce a CBDC (doc 6 p.2), so no design is adopted. The value is a tested capability only.
counter_evidence: doc 6 p.12: any participant with read access to the ledger would be able to view the entire transaction history related to this address

derivation: inferred (§6.5: (i) banks map customers to ledger addresses in own registers, doc 7 p.9; (ii) participating banks have read access to the ledger transaction history, doc 6 p.12; (iii) same retail online sandbox, same participant)
quote: Banks are responsible for customer onboarding and for linking customers to ledger addresses that are registered in the banks’ own account registers.
justification: Doc 7 p.9 documents that banks hold the identifier-to-person mapping for retail CBDC addresses. Doc 6 p.12 states that participating banks with read access can see the transaction history of a linked address. Both premises refer to the same tested retail sandbox and the same participants, so the inference is drawn. The arrangement was only tested; no design was adopted (doc 6 p.2).
counter_evidence: doc 2 p.8: Til forskjell fra en bankkonto er registeret ikke knyttet til identitet, men til kryptografiske koder og nøkler

quote: Fifth, it must be clarified who is to be responsible for transaction monitoring under the Anti-Money Laundering Act with respect to CBDCs.
justification: The documents say KYC/AML requirements would equal those for other payment services, with banks performing checks. However, the latest report leaves open who would be responsible for transaction monitoring under the AML Act; doc 5 p.15 says the same. No route by which an authority obtains person-attributable data, and no named holder for such a route, is documented. Doc 6 p.12 mentions court orders only as a privacy risk, not as a documented route.
counter_evidence: doc 6 p.16: KYC and AML checks of CBDC users would have to be performed by banks

quote: Tilfredsstiller krav til teknisk uavhengighet og mulighet for betaling offline
justification: Offline payment is listed as a required characteristic, but no offline mode was adopted. Norges Bank decided not to introduce a CBDC (doc 6 p.2). Privacy of offline transfers, including at synchronisation, is not described as a commitment; only options are discussed (doc 4 p.24, p.40). An offline mode without a privacy description is unknown.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p.24: kan anonyme forhåndsbetalte kort gi anonymitet innenfor rammene av tillatt omfang

quote: For både hovedløsningen og den alternative løsningen kan det vurderes om det bør være mulighet for begrenset tilgang for personer som ikke tilfredsstiller kravene som nevnt over, for eksempel for turister og andre som midlertidig oppholder seg i Norge.
limits: smaller amounts, possibly time-limited, at least one party fully KYC (footnote 23, option)
justification: Lower-identification routes appear only as options: tourists in doc 2 and anonymous prepaid cards in doc 4. None was adopted, and no CBDC is to be introduced (doc 6 p.2). Because other routes are mentioned, F7 = no cannot be inferred under §6.6a. No document states an explicit all-routes identification requirement.
counter_evidence: doc 6 p.16: KYC and AML checks of CBDC users would have to be performed by banks

quote: KYC and AML checks of CBDC users would have to be performed by banks or other market participants that offer wallets for CBDC storage and transactions to their customers.
justification: The latest report lists KYC checks by wallet-providing banks as a design feature for a retail CBDC. Doc 2 p.26 similarly links access to the same requirements as opening a Norwegian bank account. The report calls this list a rough draft, and no CBDC is to be introduced, so the status is option.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p.24: kan anonyme forhåndsbetalte kort gi anonymitet innenfor rammene av tillatt omfang

quote: vil likevel innebære at det må gjøres koblinger mellom «tokens» og identitet, for eksempel ved on-boarding av nye brukere, store transaksjoner og mistenkelige transaksjoner.
modality: conditional: onboarding, large or suspicious transactions
justification: For a pseudonymous token design, the working group states that customer-control requirements imply token-identity links for large and suspicious transactions. Doc 4 p.38 also mentions keys that authorised actors can unlock under procedures. This is an option in a design that was never adopted (doc 6 p.2).

quote: CBDC should not be programmable money, and programmability, if implemented, should be at the payment service level.
justification: The latest report's draft design features exclude programmability at the money level and confine it to payment services. Earlier, doc 4 p.41 discussed purpose-bound social support only as a possibility and urged caution. The design is a rough draft and is not adopted, so the status is option.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p.41: det kunne programmeres inn at ulike former for sosial støtte bare kan brukes dersom visse begivenheter inntrer

quote: The purpose of the Bank's research project is to assess whether the introduction of CBDC is appropriate to ensure that it is secure, efficient and attractive to pay with NOK also in the future.
justification: The project's declared purpose is a secure, efficient and attractive payment system in NOK. Doc 6 p.2 restates the same aim.

quote: Introducing a retail CBDC is not a suitable measure for financial inclusion in Norway.
justification: Norges Bank explicitly rejects financial inclusion as a rationale for a Norwegian CBDC. Inclusion appears in the documents only as the ECB's motive, not Norway's.

quote: The two most important risks in Norges Bank's areas of responsibility are linked to currency substitution away from NOK and diminished national control over the payment system.
justification: The precautionary motivation rests on currency substitution and national control over the payment system. Doc 2 p.6 and doc 6 p.7 support this. Doc 5 states that CBDC is not a monetary policy instrument, but sovereignty and national control are declared motives.
counter_evidence: doc 5 p.8: with respect to the precautionary approach, introducing retail CBDC is not a very urgent matter

quote: Norges Banks utredning er motivert av lav og fallende kontantbruk og hensynet til å være «føre var».
justification: Falling cash use and the preservation of cash properties, including independent contingency, are declared motivations across docs 1–6. Doc 6 p.5 assesses contingency as a declared objective while finding it not currently decisive.
counter_evidence: doc 6 p.5: contingency considerations do not at present provide a decisive argument for the introduction of a retail CBDC

quote: KYC and AML checks of CBDC users would have to be performed by banks or other market participants that offer wallets for CBDC storage and transactions to their customers.
justification: AML appears only as a design requirement, not as a declared objective. Doc 4 p.43 reports some authorities' wish for traceability and taxation, but Norges Bank does not adopt it as an objective. The zero flag means not documented.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p.43: noen myndigheter vekt på at DSP utformes slik at det er enkelt å spore opp pengenes opprinnelse

quote: Introducing a CBDC can be a way to ensure access to a means of settlement trusted by all, also in new payment arenas, and can also facilitate responsible innovation and improved payment contingency arrangements.
justification: Innovation and competition in payments are declared objectives. Doc 2 p.6 cites competition, and doc 6 p.5 places particular emphasis on payment innovation.

quote: Norges Bank has placed particular emphasis on whether the introduction of a CBDC could promote innovation in payment services and whether it would be a suitable instrument to strengthen contingency arrangements in Norway's payment system.
justification: The latest report jointly emphasises payment innovation and contingency. The 2018 memo had named a single main purpose, trust in money and the monetary system. That earlier ranking is treated as superseded by the 2026 report.
counter_evidence: doc 1 p.4: Hovedformålet er å sørge for tillit til penger og pengevesenet.

value: innovation in payment services and payment contingency/preparedness (joint emphasis), within the overarching aim that NOK remains an efficient, attractive and secure means of payment
quote: Norges Bank has placed particular emphasis on whether the introduction of a CBDC could promote innovation in payment services and whether it would be a suitable instrument to strengthen contingency arrangements in Norway's payment system.
justification: The jointly emphasised objectives are taken from the latest report. The 2018 single main purpose (trust in money) is superseded.
counter_evidence: doc 1 p.4: Hovedformålet er å sørge for tillit til penger og pengevesenet.

quote: The sandbox solution in this test case is based on Hyperledger Besu, which is a permissioned ledger compatible with the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM)
transaction_scope: online core (retail Besu; wholesale Hyperledger Fabric)
justification: Phase 5 tested permissioned Hyperledger Besu and Fabric sandboxes; earlier, a private Ethereum network was used in phase 4. Doc 6 p.17 states the ledger 'should probably' be blockchain-based and, for wholesale, initially private. That remains an option, since no CBDC is to be introduced. The earlier position of no preferred technology (doc 3 p.7) is superseded only by tested and option claims.
counter_evidence: doc 6 p.4: In principle, retail CBDC can rely on traditional technologies
